class.name: Controller
class.brief_description: Base class for anything that can possess a [Pawn].
class.description: Holds the possession relationship. See [PlayerController] for the player-facing subclass. Controllers add themselves to [method World.get_controllers] from [code]_enter_tree[/code] and take themselves out again in [code]_exit_tree[/code], so the world list also picks up AI controllers and controllers a designer placed in a level by hand, and can never hold a freed one. [b]A subclass that overrides [code]_enter_tree[/code] or [code]_exit_tree[/code] must call the base implementation[/b], or it will never be registered - Godot binds only the most derived override.

method.name: _on_possess
method.description: Override to react to taking a pawn. The argument is always the possessed [Pawn]; it is typed as [Node] because a virtual's argument types have to be complete.

method.name: _on_unpossess
method.description: Override to react to letting a pawn go.

method.name: get_local_role
method.description: What this peer may do with this controller - see [enum World.NetRole].

method.name: get_owner_peer_id
method.description: Which connection this controller answers to. A remote call arriving from anyone else is dropped. Everything driven by the server answers to the server.

method.name: get_pawn
method.description: The [Pawn] node currently possessed, or null.

method.name: get_pawn_root
method.description: The node the pawn scene is rooted at - the [RigidBody2D] or [CharacterBody3D] a game actually moves around, rather than the [Pawn] marker inside it. This is what gameplay code usually wants.

method.name: get_player_id
method.description: The server-assigned id this controller and its pawn are named after, and how the same player is found on every peer.

method.name: get_player_state
method.description: This player's replicated data. It lives under the [GameStateBase], not here: a controller exists only on the server and on its own client, while a player state has to be visible everywhere.

method.name: get_world
method.description: The world this controller belongs to. Null when the project does not use [World] as its main loop.

method.name: has_authority
method.description: True on the server, and in a game with no peer at all - which is what lets a rule written for a server also be correct offline.

method.name: is_local_controller
method.description: True where this controller's decisions are actually made - on the server for an [AIController], on the owning client for a player.

method.name: is_player_controller
method.description: False here, true on a [PlayerController]. It is what tells a bot's pawn from a human's without reaching for a cast.

method.name: possess
method.description: Takes control of [param pawn]: sets the pawn's controller, calls [method Pawn._possessed] and [method _on_possess], and on a [PlayerController] builds the [InputComponent] and calls [method Pawn._setup_input_component]. Possessing while already possessing something releases the old pawn first.

method.name: set_player_id
method.description: Sets the id. Handed out by the server on login; a project does not assign it.

method.name: set_player_state
method.description: Points this controller at its player state. The framework does this on login.

method.name: unpossess
method.description: Lets the current pawn go. The pawn stays in the world; only the will behind it is gone.

signal.name: pawn_changed
signal.description: The possessed pawn changed, including to null on unpossession.

signal.name: player_state_changed
signal.description: This controller was pointed at a different player state.
